title: Universe enlargement compatible with enriched tensor comparison
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'\in\mathcal U''$ and use [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and [lem-coef-cocomplete-monoidal-tensor]. Let $V,W$ be $\mathcal U'$-small monoidal infinity categories with all $\mathcal U$-small colimits, whose tensors preserve these colimits separately. After increasing $\mathcal U'$ if necessary to contain the cocomplete tensor $V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc},\mathcal U}W$, there are $\mathcal U'$-presentably monoidal infinity categories $\widehat V,\widehat W$ and fully faithful strong monoidal embeddings
$$j_V:V\hookrightarrow\widehat V,\quad j_W:W\hookrightarrow\widehat W,\quad j_{VW}:V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc},\mathcal U}W\hookrightarrow\widehat V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc},\mathcal U'}\widehat W$$
preserving $\mathcal U$-small colimits and satisfying $j_{VW}\mu\simeq\widehat\mu(j_V\times j_W)$. The embeddings $j_V,j_W$ may be chosen as Yoneda embeddings into $\mathcal U'$-space-valued presheaves on $V,W$, respectively, localized at the arrows $\operatorname{colim}_K y(p)\to y(\operatorname{colim}_Kp)$ for all $\mathcal U$-small diagrams $p$; the latter is a $\mathcal U'$-small collection after enlargement. The embedding $j_{VW}$ is the induced fully faithful map from the smaller-universe cocomplete tensor into the larger-universe tensor of these two localized presheaf categories. No local $\mathcal U$-smallness hypothesis on $V,W$ is imposed. In this notation $\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U}$ means that object spaces are $\mathcal U$-small. The induced functors
$$J_V:\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U}(V)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U'}(\widehat V),\quad J_W:\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U}(W)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U'}(\widehat W),$$
$$J_{VW}:\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U}(V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc},\mathcal U}W)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U'}(\widehat V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc},\mathcal U'}\widehat W)$$
are fully faithful and preserve $\mathcal U$-small colimits. They satisfy a coherent equivalence
$$J_{VW}\bigl(\mu_*(A\boxtimes B)\bigr)\simeq\widehat\mu_*(J_VA\boxtimes J_WB).$$
All the displayed larger categories are formed in $\mathcal U''$.

source.place: Section 9, all paragraphs preceding Corollary 9.1; Higher Algebra section 4.8.1 (localized-presheaf construction of the cocomplete tensor); online source, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal K=\{\mathcal U\text{-small simplicial shapes}\}$ and $\mathcal K'=\{\mathcal U'\text{-small simplicial shapes}\}$. Enlarge $\mathcal U'$ to contain $T=V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc},\mathcal U}W$, as permitted in the statement. Each of $V,W,T$ is then small in $\mathcal U'$, including its mapping spaces. The collection of all $\mathcal U$-small shapes, functors from them to one of these three categories, and their chosen colimit cocones is a set in $\mathcal U'$: its simplices are subsets and maps of sets in $\mathcal U'$, and the shapes range over the set $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$. Choose one colimit cocone for each diagram. Thus the relations below form $\mathcal U'$-small sets. No assertion of local $\mathcal U$-smallness is involved.

For $C=V,W$, let $R_C$ be the set of chosen $\mathcal U$-small colimit cocones from step 1. Apply relative free cocompletion with small meaning $\mathcal U'$-small, and put $\widehat C=P_{R_C}(C)$. Since $C,R_C$ are $\mathcal U'$-small, the theorem realizes this as the presentable localization of $P_{\mathcal U'}(C)$ at $s_p:\operatorname{colim}yp\to y(\operatorname{colim}p)$. Its map $j_C=Ly$ sends $R_C$ to colimit cocones, hence preserves all $\mathcal U$-small colimits. For $c\in C$ the mapping-space criterion gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{P(C)}(y(\operatorname{colim}p),y(c))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(\operatorname{colim}p,c)\simeq\lim_k\operatorname{Map}_C(p(k),c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{P(C)}(\operatorname{colim}yp,y(c)).$$
Thus each representable is local. The reflector unit on a local object is an equivalence, so full inclusion of local objects and full faithfulness of Yoneda give $\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat C}(Ly(c),Ly(d))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{P(C)}(y(c),y(d))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(c,d)$. Hence $j_C$ is fully faithful. Write $S_C=\{s_p:p\in R_C\}$ for the set of presheaf arrows, distinct from the cocone set $R_C$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.2, with K all enlarged-universe small shapes and R all original-universe colimit cocones

proof.text: For $C=V,W$, apply the monoidal Yoneda theorem at $\mathcal U'$: $P_{\mathcal U'}(C)$ is presentably monoidal and $y:C\to P_{\mathcal U'}(C)$ is coherently strong monoidal. In particular $y(c)\otimes_{\mathrm{Day}}y(d)\simeq y(c\otimes d)$, with its unit and higher compatibilities. Apply the tensor-stable-cocone compatibility lemma to the family $R_C$ of step 2. Indeed, tensoring a chosen $\mathcal U$-small colimit cocone on either side gives another colimit cocone of that size, because tensor on $C$ preserves those colimits separately. It is equivalent to the chosen cocone for that tensor diagram, so the lemma's closure-up-to-equivalence hypothesis holds. The relation family $S_C$ is $\mathcal U'$-small by step 1. The lemma therefore says exactly that $S_C$ is monoidally compatible, including tensoring its generators with arbitrary presheaves. The localization-model theorem now gives $P^{S_C}(C)$ a monoidal reflective localization with strong monoidal reflector. Its underlying category is $\widehat C$ of step 2, since it has the same local objects. Composing its strong reflector with strong Yoneda makes $j_C=Ly$ strong monoidal, as required for $j_V,j_W$.

source.place: Section 9, strong monoidal vertical maps; Day convolution and monoidal localizations as in Sections 4 and 8

proof.text:
Let $R$ in $V\times W$ consist of a cocone from $R_V$ with an arbitrary fixed object of $W$, or a cocone from $R_W$ with an arbitrary fixed object of $V$. Put $H=P_R(V\times W)$, using $\mathcal U'$-small colimits for this relative free cocompletion, and denote its generator by $q$. Let $R_T$ consist of all chosen $\mathcal U$-small colimit cocones in $T$, and put $E=P_{R_T}(T)$, again completing under $\mathcal U'$-small colimits. These are small-data completions by step 1. The generator $e:T\to E$ preserves $\mathcal U$-small colimits. For $t\in T$, the formula $\operatorname{Map}_T(\operatorname{colim}p,t)\simeq\lim_k\operatorname{Map}_T(p(k),t)$ makes $y(t)$ local for every relation of $R_T$. Consequently $e=Ly$ has mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_E(e(t),e(t'))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{P(T)}(y(t),y(t'))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_T(t,t')$, so is fully faithful. For every $\mathcal U'$-cocomplete $Z$, relative completion and the smaller-universe tensor universal property give
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim},\mathcal U'}(E,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim},\mathcal U}(T,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{sep\ colim},\mathcal U}(V\times W,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{R}(V\times W,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim},\mathcal U'}(H,Z).$$
Here the middle equality holds because $R$ prescribes precisely the original colimits separately in each variable. Explicitly, $q$ factors through a $\mathcal U$-cocontinuous $T\to H$, which extends to $E\to H$; $e\mu$ sends $R$ to colimits and extends to $H\to E$. Each composite restricts to the identity on its generators, so full faithfulness of the displayed restriction equivalences identifies these composites with the identities, including the coherent compatibility data. We obtain $E\simeq H$, taking $e\mu$ to $q$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.2 and the n=1 universal-property comparison underlying Proposition 5.3.6.11; explicit comparison written here

proof.text:
Put $S=\widehat V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc},\mathcal U'}\widehat W$. Apply the finite-variable clause of relative free cocompletion at $\mathcal U'$ to $(V,R_V),(W,R_W)$. For every $\mathcal U'$-cocomplete $Z$, it gives, together with the larger-universe tensor property,
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim},\mathcal U'}(S,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{sep\ colim},\mathcal U'}(\widehat V\times\widehat W,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_R(V\times W,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim},\mathcal U'}(H,Z).$$
The functor $b=\widehat\mu(j_V\times j_W)$ sends each member of $R$ to a colimit, since $j_V,j_W$ preserve the original small colimits and $\widehat\mu$ preserves enlarged colimits separately. It therefore extends to $h:H\to S$ preserving enlarged colimits. Conversely the finite-variable equivalence extends $q$ to a separately enlarged-cocontinuous $\widehat V\times\widehat W\to H$, which factors through an enlarged-cocontinuous $S\to H$. The two composites restrict to the identities on $V\times W$; full faithfulness in the displayed chain identifies them with the identities and identifies all restriction compatibilities. Thus $h$ is an equivalence with $hq\simeq b$. Define $j_{VW}$ as $T\xrightarrow{e}E\simeq H\xrightarrow{h}S$. It is fully faithful and preserves $\mathcal U$-small colimits; the generator comparisons give $j_{VW}\mu\simeq\widehat\mu(j_V\times j_W)$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.11, finite-variable restriction equivalence, applied to all enlarged-universe small colimits; comparison maps and inverse identities written here

proof.text: Put $S=\widehat V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc},\mathcal U'}\widehat W$ and $b=\widehat\mu(j_V\times j_W)$. The functor $b$ is strong monoidal, as a composite of strong monoidal functors, and preserves $\mathcal U$-small colimits separately. The monoidal clause of the cocomplete-tensor theorem, applied to $V,W,S$ with small meaning $\mathcal U$-small, gives a strong monoidal colimit-preserving factor $k:T\to S$ and a coherent monoidal equivalence $k\mu\simeq b$. Step 5 gives a colimit-preserving $j_{VW}:T\to S$ with $j_{VW}\mu\simeq b$. Since restriction along $\mu$ is an equivalence of infinity categories of these functors, it lifts the resulting equivalence $j_{VW}\mu\simeq k\mu$ to a coherent natural equivalence $\alpha:j_{VW}\simeq k$, compatible with the specified restriction. Define the tensor comparison for $j_{VW}$ as the composite $j_{VW}(t)\otimes j_{VW}(t')\xrightarrow{\alpha_t\otimes\alpha_{t'}}k(t)\otimes k(t')\simeq k(t\otimes t')\xrightarrow{\alpha_{t\otimes t'}^{-1}}j_{VW}(t\otimes t')$; define its unit comparison by $\mathbf1_S\simeq k(\mathbf1_T)\xrightarrow{\alpha_{\mathbf1_T}^{-1}}j_{VW}(\mathbf1_T)$. The associativity, unit and higher coherence homotopies are those of $k$, composed with $\alpha$ and its inverse; their compatibility follows from the coherent inverse identities of $\alpha$. This makes $j_{VW}$ strong monoidal and makes the square with $\mu$ and $\widehat\mu$ a coherent monoidal square.

source.place: Section 9 strong monoidal comparison; Higher Algebra Proposition 4.8.1.3 and Remark 4.8.1.8 (coherent cocomplete-tensor universal property)

proof.text: For each of the three embeddings $j:C\to\widehat C$, postcomposition gives a fully faithful functor $j_*:\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U}(C)\to\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U}(\widehat C)$. To check this, replace $C$ by its full monoidal essential image. For fixed object spaces $X,Y$ and fixed map $f:X\to Y$, an algebra transformation $jA\to f^*jB$ is exactly a transformation $A\to f^*B$: all its operation maps and higher coherence simplices lie between objects of the full monoidal subcategory, so the two spaces of such data coincide. The space of possible maps $f$ is unchanged. This proves full faithfulness on the entire algebroid mapping space, not merely on homotopy classes. The cocontinuous-change-of-enrichment theorem, applied with small meaning $\mathcal U$-small, gives existence of colimits and preservation of all $\mathcal U$-small colimits by these three $j_*$, including the empty colimit.

source.place: Section 9 induced vertical algebroid functors; composition of operadic algebras and cocontinuous change of enrichment

proof.text:
It remains to enlarge object spaces. For a presentably monoidal $E$ in $\mathcal U'$, its terminal object $1_E$ exists. For every space $X$ the algebroid $I_E(X)$ with object space $X$ and every mapping object $1_E$ exists: every operation to $1_E$ and every coherence has a contractible space of choices. The definition of algebroid morphisms gives $\operatorname{Map}(A,I_E(X))\simeq\operatorname{Map}(\operatorname{Ob}A,X)$. For a diagram $A:K\to\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U'}(E)$, its colimit $L$ exists by cocontinuous change of enrichment, applied at $\mathcal U'$. For every $X\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$, the preceding natural equivalence and the colimit universal property give
$$\operatorname{Map}(\operatorname{Ob}L,X)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(L,I_E(X))\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(A_k,I_E(X))\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(\operatorname{Ob}A_k,X).$$
These equivalences take the maps of the object-space cocone to its restriction maps. Thus the cocone $\operatorname{Ob}A\to\operatorname{Ob}L$ is colimiting by the mapping-space criterion; this proves that $\operatorname{Ob}$ preserves colimits. For a $\mathcal U$-small diagram whose object spaces are $\mathcal U$-small, the enlarged colimit has object space $\operatorname{colim}X_k$, still essentially $\mathcal U$-small by universe absoluteness of space colimits. Thus the full subcategory on these object spaces is closed under such colimits. It is precisely $\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U}(E)$, since all the operadic algebra and mapping-space data are unchanged. Its fully faithful inclusion into $\operatorname{Algd}_{\mathcal U'}(E)$ therefore preserves these colimits. Apply this to $E=\widehat V,\widehat W,\widehat V\otimes\widehat W$, which are all presentably monoidal. Composing with step 7 proves all three assertions about $J_V,J_W,J_{VW}$.

source.place: Section 9 change of object-space universe; explicit terminal-mapping-object adjunction; HTT 4.2.4 homotopy colimits of spaces

proof.text: Finally the external product is natural under change of enrichment, has object space $X\times Y$, and its operation maps are the pairs of operation maps of $A,B$. The coherent monoidal square $j_{VW}\mu\simeq\widehat\mu(j_V\times j_W)$ from steps 5–6 therefore gives the displayed equivalence of algebroids by postcomposition. On mapping objects both sides are identified by $j_{VW}\mu(A(x,x'),B(y,y'))\simeq\widehat\mu(j_VA(x,x'),j_WB(y,y'))$; the monoidal square identifies the units, composition and all higher coherences. Since $X\times Y$ is still $\mathcal U$-small, enlarging its universe does not alter this identification. All presheaf, localized, tensor and algebroid categories constructed above fit in $\mathcal U''$ after the permitted size choices.

source.place: Section 9 commutative algebroid square; Corollary 3.2 and functoriality of external product
